description: We’re a team of passionate student developers interested in space, technology, AI/ML, and creative problem-solving. We’re looking for teammates who can contribute with coding, research, UI/UX, data analysis, or innovative ideas. Let’s build something impactful for the NASA Space Apps Challenge!
summary: The Tale of NASA's Forgotten Legacy is an interactive 3D storytelling experience that brings NASA's lesser-known space missions back to life. Through immersive environments, realistic 3D models, cinematic animations and narrated stories, visitors can explore the machines and missions that shaped space exploration, from the Moon landings to Mars rovers and the Kepler telescope. Our goal is to make space history more engaging, accessible and memorable through an experience that feels like exploring a documentary rather than reading one.
details:
"The Tale of NASA's Forgotten Legacy" is a scroll-driven, interactive 3D storytelling web experience built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It tells the stories of humanity's silent explorers left across the Solar System — from the surface of the Moon and Mars to deep heliocentric orbit — featuring historic hardware including the Apollo 11 Laser Ranging Retroreflector (1969), the Opportunity Rover (2004), and the Kepler Space Telescope (2009–2018). The narrative is structured into an episodic, five-chapter learning arc designed specifically for students aged 10–15.

How it works: As users scroll, they journey through dynamic, real-scale 3D scenes: traversing real NASA planetary globes, tracking Kepler’s Earth-trailing heliocentric orbit, and inspecting authentic 3D spacecraft and rover models with interactive hotspots. Synchronized with the user's scroll progression, an AI-generated cinematic voiceover narrates the story in real time — powered by Google Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS — delivering each chapter with context-aware emotional profiles (historical awe, Martian suspense, contemplative solitude, and scientific inspiration). The system features automatic background music ducking, intelligent pre-fetching, and disk caching for zero-latency playback. Each story concludes with an open scientific question, and students can collect hypotheses in their own local "Question Constellation" without accounts or tracking.

Benefits and impact: The project brings decades of NASA astrophysics and planetary exploration alive for young learners by distinguishing confirmed facts, scientific inferences, and still-unanswered questions. Introducing the Kepler Space Telescope transforms the narrative from surface landings to the hunt for habitable alien worlds, helping students understand planetary transit science and orbital mechanics. The synchronized audio narration removes reading hurdles for younger students, while a printable teacher page allows educators to integrate the experience directly into classroom curricula.

Tools and technologies used:

  • Languages: TypeScript, HTML, CSS
  • Framework: React 18 with Vite
  • 3D Graphics: Three.js via React Three Fiber, Drei, and custom postprocessing pipelines (lazy-loaded after initial paint)
  • Animation & Scrolling: GSAP with ScrollTrigger, Framer Motion, and Lenis smooth scrolling
  • AI Narration Engine: Google Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS with emotion-tuned delivery profiles, audio ducking, cross-fades, and a Vercel serverless backend
  • Data Validation: Ajv with JSON Schema (automated build checks enforce that all mission facts cite official nasa.gov sources)
  • Hosting: Vercel (static front-end with serverless API routes)
  • 3D Models: NASA 3D Resources, JPL-Caltech telemetry models, Smithsonian Institution scans, and CC-BY community models

Creativity: Rather than a static catalog, each mission's narrative, 3D camera staging, and voiceover pacing are driven seamlessly by structured data. The project highlights human engineering resilience — showcasing how Kepler was given a second life through solar radiation pressure after reaction wheel failures. Data integrity is enforced as code: builds automatically fail if NASA source URLs or verification tags are missing. The application also provides complete accessibility fallback to high-resolution NASA imagery on devices without WebGL and respects prefers-reduced-motion preferences.
